context: Multi-panel tidal harmonic decomposition showing a 14-day synthetic composite signal (M2, S2, K1, O1 constituents) with a main time-series, a cycle plot overlaying daily patterns, and a ridgeline KDE of amplitude distributions per constituent.
first_impression: Structurally honest line-chart dashboard with toggleable harmonics, data-driven time axis, and a well-chosen KDE bandwidth — held back from higher scores by hardcoded Y-domains and a KDE that slightly smooths the bimodal distribution inherent to sinusoidal amplitudes.
what_works: Time-axis domain uses d3.extent (data-driven); Silverman/Scott bandwidth rule applied to the Epanechnikov KDE in the ridgeline; cycle-plot day-overlay uses a key function (d => d.dayIdx) preventing identity corruption on updates.
what_doesnt: Y-axes on main and cycle plots are hardcoded at [-2.8, 2.8] rather than derived from data, making the chart brittle under amplitude scaling (fails the scaling metamorphic relation); ridgeline KDE applies a unimodal-optimised bandwidth to sinusoidal data whose true amplitude distribution is bimodal (peaks near ±amplitude), mildly obscuring that structure.
